title: A cluster randomized controlled trial of a school-based vaping and smoking prevention intervention aimed at schoolchildren in Grade 5
summary: This study examines the effects of a school-based vaping and smoking prevention program on motivation, smoking and vaping in school children in Year 5. Children receiving the three-workshop program will be compared to children receiving the standard curriculum at their school. All children are surveyed again 3, 6 and 12 months after the first survey. The data from the 12-month survey will be used to assess whether the program is effective in motivating children to live a smoke- and vape-free life.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders due to use of tobacco: Dependence syndrome

interventions.name:
Intervention group: Three interactive workshops in the classroom, each 3 months apart, led by members of the study team with a background in psychology, human medicine or health sciences. 
Workshop 1: 180 minutes, alternatively split into two separate 90-minute sessions: Topics: Health consequences

Active control: Standard curriculum taught by class teachers, which is meant to cover the prevention of addiction and tobacco use.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Schools in the Berlin districts of Neukölln, Mitte, Reinickendorf, Lichtenberg, Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg and Spandau will be included in the study. The eligible schools included elementary school and comprehensive schools with grades 5 and 6. 
Grade 5 classes will be eligible to be enrolled (thus, age of individual students may vary). 
Schools with mixed-grade classes (i.e., classes that are usually being taught in age-mixed groups) will be included in the study provided that new class groups will be formed for the teaching of the prevention program (only 5th and 6th graders). In order to include individual students from a participating school class in the study, informed written consent for data collection will be required from both the students and their parents.
Exclusion criteria:
Schools are required to provide written consent not to engage other external providers for smoking prevention among the target group of 5th graders.  If schools should refuse to consent to it, they must at least agree to notify the study team of any external providers involved in smoking prevention work with the classes.  Schools that are unwilling to agree to either of those conditions (abstain or notify) will not be included in the study.
